entries.title: Variance scaling does not determine exponential-tail scaling
entries.statement: DRAFT audit concept; scoped argument independently checked by w374 (KEEP). For the centered symmetric family with masses (1-1/n)/2 at +/-n^(1/3) and 1/(2n) at +/-n^(2/3), the lower variance exponent is 1/3 while the uniform upper exponential-moment exponent is 2/3. This is an abstract family, not FPP; it refutes inferring the strong upper exponent solely from the variance exponent.
assumptions: Integer n>=2; exponent definitions are the analogous all-n moment thresholds, not FPP exponents.

entries.title: Selecting a geodesic couples disjoint route costs
entries.statement: DRAFT audit concept; scoped argument independently checked by w374 (KEEP). On a four-edge square graph with iid Uniform[1,2] weights and opposite-corner endpoints, let A,B be its two route costs. Conditional on A<B, P(A<=3)=P(B>=3)=3/4 and P(A<=3,B>=3)=1/2; the conditional product 9/16 is false. The iid disjoint route costs are independent before conditioning; conditioning on which route wins destroys that independence. Deterministic restricted domains computed without such conditioning remain a valid independence route.
assumptions: Finite square graph only; disjoint two-edge routes; iid continuous Uniform[1,2]; condition on the top route being the unique geodesic.

entries.title: Bounded positive FPP has zero wandering at a short endpoint
entries.statement: DRAFT audit concept; scoped argument independently checked by w374 (KEEP). For nearest-neighbor FPP on Z^d, d>=2, with every edge weight in [1,2], D(0,e1)=0 for every environment, so a strictly positive lower bound inf_{v!=0} ED(0,v)/|v|^b>0 is impossible for any real b. The direct edge costs at most 2 while every alternative simple path costs at least 3. This does not refute an asymptotic lower wandering bound with a sufficiently-large-distance cutoff.
assumptions: Undirected nearest-neighbor lattice; positive bounded weights in [1,2]; D is maximum distance of a minimizing path from the endpoint segment.

entries.title: High-probability cost agreement does not transfer variance
entries.statement: DRAFT audit concept; scoped argument independently checked by w374 (KEEP). High-probability agreement of costs in [n,2n] does not imply variance transfer: T_n=n and Y_n=n+nB_n with B_n Bernoulli(1/n) agree with probability 1-1/n but have Var T_n=0, Var Y_n=n-1, and E(Y_n-T_n)^2=n. A cylinder localization probability must be paired with an L2 discrepancy small relative to the true standard deviation. No FPP realization or impossibility result is claimed.
assumptions: Integer n>=2; abstract cost coupling, not a constructed FPP environment.

entries.title: Lattice symmetry and norm bounds do not force axial curvature
entries.statement: DRAFT audit concept; independent mathematical review pending. The norm g(x)=max(||x||_1,(3/2)||x||_infinity) has square-lattice symmetries and ||x||_1<=g(x)<=(3/2)||x||_1, yet for even n and w+1<=n/4, z=(n/2,w+1) gives g(z)+g(ne1-z)-g(ne1)=0 outside the width-w cylinder. The maximum of these two norms is a norm, but it has a flat axial face. A quadratic mean-gap route needs FPP-specific curvature, and nonrandom-error control when replacing actual means by the norm; this norm is not asserted to be an FPP limit shape.
assumptions: A norm countermodel on R^2; n even and w>=1 integer; no realization as an iid FPP time constant is claimed.
